title: Question 14748
subject: Criminal Law & Procedure
stem:
Barnabas entered the Christian law school’s Bible manuscript gallery while it was open to visitors, intending to steal Lydia’s original hand-lettered Psalm 23 page. Once inside, Barnabas took what he thought was the original page from an unlocked display case and tucked it inside his jacket. However, the page in the case was a photocopy; Lydia’s original had been loaned to another school for an exhibit. A sign above the display case said that similar photocopies were available free at the front desk. Barnabas did not see the sign. Burglary in the jurisdiction is defined as “entering a building unlawfully with the intent to commit a crime.”

Barnabas is guilty of:
rightExplanation:
C is correct. Barnabas took and concealed the display copy while intending to steal. The fact that the page was a photocopy, not the original, does not downgrade the completed taking into an attempt.

Gold Key: A completed theft is not downgraded to attempt just because the thief got a less valuable or different item than expected. Once another’s property is taken with steal-intent, the completed theft label controls.

Silver Key: Split the answer labels into two axes: first, burglary or no burglary; second, larceny or attempted larceny. Do not process the whole label at once.

wrongExplanations.A: It correctly keeps larceny, but it adds burglary. The stem gives the burglary definition: unlawful entry plus intent. Barnabas entered while the gallery was open to visitors. That cuts burglary.
wrongExplanations.B: The free-copy sign is the trap. Barnabas did not see it, and he took the display copy while intending to steal. Gold Key: the wrong-object / lower-value fact does not erase the completed theft.
wrongExplanations.D: This is the dominant trap. Barnabas did not merely try and fail. He actually took the display copy. Gold Key: attempt merges into the completed theft when the target offense is completed. Silver Key: once C and D are the last fight pair, ask whether the taking happened, not whether he got the exact thing he wanted.

c3.label: CUT A
c3.text: “burglary and larceny” contains the right theft label but adds burglary. The entry fact does not match the burglary definition. Cut the extra crime.

c3.label: CUT B
c3.text: “no crime” overreacts to the free-copy sign. Barnabas did not see the sign and took the display copy with steal-intent. Cut the no-crime answer.

c3.label: CLASH C vs. D
c3.text: The fight is completed larceny vs. attempted larceny.

c3.label: CALL
c3.text: Apply the tiny anchor. He actually took the display copy. Completed theft beats attempt. C remains.

studentScript: Cut burglary because the gallery was open. Cut no crime because he took the display copy with steal-intent. Clash C and D: completed theft or attempt. He actually took property, so call larceny.

A.signal: It keeps the theft label but adds a second crime whose entry requirement does not match the open-gallery fact.
A.lawyer: No burglary because the entry was lawful under the supplied burglary definition. Larceny portion is correct.

B.signal: The answer treats the free-copy sign as erasing the taking, but the stem says Barnabas did not see the sign and took the display copy with steal-intent.
B.lawyer: Completed larceny remains because he took another's property with intent to steal.

C.lawyer: Correct under the official explanation and common larceny elements.

D.signal: It notices the wrong object, but stops at attempt even though the display copy was actually taken.
D.lawyer: Attempt merges into the completed larceny when the taking is complete.

goldKeys.statement: When burglary is defined as unlawful entry plus intent, intent to steal does not make a public, permitted entry unlawful.
goldKeys.trigger: The stem defines burglary with 'entering unlawfully' and says the place was open to visitors.

goldKeys.statement: If the defendant actually takes another's property with steal-intent, the crime is completed larceny even if the item is a copy or less valuable than expected; attempt merges.
goldKeys.trigger: The defendant took a displayed copy while intending to steal an original.
goldKeys.unlocks: D attempted-larceny trap and B no-crime trap.
goldKeys.authority: Official explanation plus common larceny elements and attempt-merger principle.

silverKeys.statement: When choices are only crime labels, split each label into axes. First ask whether burglary survives; then ask whether the theft was completed or only attempted.
silverKeys.trigger: Short answer choices listing combinations of crimes.
silverKeys.unlocks: Crime-label quartet with burglary and attempt traps.

remediation.title: Wrong object does not automatically mean attempt.
remediation.signal: The defendant got a copy, fake, or lower-value object.
remediation.studentMove: Ask whether any property was actually taken with steal-intent.
remediation.tinyRule: Completed taking controls over the wrong-object instinct.
